procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home, verbal consent.

Buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 BID, no opioid use. Holidays were rough, spent a lot of time with family and "wasn't on top of things," admits he missed a stretch of his HIV pills in December, back on them the last week or so. HIV clinic visit is in February.

No fevers, no weight loss he's noticed.
PDMP reviewed. UDS at next in-person visit.

Plan: buprenorphine 4-week Rx x2. Pillbox and phone alarm for the ART. Let ID know at his visit. In person in March.

documents.title: HIV clinic follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Infectious Disease / HIV Clinic
Visit date: 02/11/2026
Re: Brandon Crowley

He reports missing ART for several weeks over the holidays, restarted mid-January. No new symptoms.

Meds: bictegravir/FTC/TAF daily; buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg BID; naloxone PRN. Allergies: NKDA.

Labs today: HIV-1 RNA 7,400 copies/mL, CD4 228 (from <20 and 371 in July).

Assessment: viremia from the adherence gap, already back on therapy for about four weeks. Bictegravir has a high barrier to resistance; no change in regimen. Adherence counseling done; pharmacy blister packs arranged. Repeat viral load in 3 months.

documents.title: Re: HIV clinic labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Brandon, I saw the HIV clinic note. The virus came back up while you were off the pills, which is what we'd expect, and it should come back down now that you're taking them every day. Let's talk about what helps you stay on track when I see you March 27.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for bup follow-up and to go over the HIV clinic visit. Using the blister packs, says he hasn't missed a dose since mid-January. No opioid use in almost a year; cravings rare. Work picking back up. No fever, cough or night sweats. Smoking a pack a day.

O: vitals normal, weight 72 kg. Well-appearing. No thrush, no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Joints normal. Skin no new injection sites.
PHQ-9 4. UDS bup +, otherwise negative. PDMP reviewed.

A/P
1. HIV with recent viremia after a gap in ART; back on bictegravir/FTC/TAF with blister packs. ID rechecking VL in May. Reinforced.
2. OUD in early remission on buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 BID: continue, monthly refills.
3. Routine CBC and CMP today.
4. Tobacco: not ready, advised.

RTC 2-3 months; physical due in August.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood counts and chemistries normal. No action needed.

documents.title: Buprenorphine/naloxone refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Refill request from pharmacy. PDMP reviewed, fills on time. Buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg film BID, #56, sent.

results.test: Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA, cerebrospinal fluid

results.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex isolated; susceptible to isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol and pyrazinamide

reports.text: Noncontrast images followed by post-contrast images through the brain. The lateral and third ventricles are mildly enlarged, with rounding of the temporal horns. Enhancement of the basal meninges around the suprasellar cistern and brainstem on post-contrast images. No territorial infarct. No hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Calvarium and visualized sinuses unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Mild hydrocephalus and basilar meningeal enhancement. No evidence of stroke.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Lungs clear without consolidation, nodule or cavity. No hilar or mediastinal adenopathy. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal.
Comparison 05/05/2026. Ventricular size is unchanged, mildly enlarged. No new hemorrhage or infarct. No mass effect.

documents.title: Discharge Summary: tuberculous meningitis
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Community teaching hospital, Infectious Disease service
Admitted 05/05/2026 (ICU), floor 05/13, discharged 05/29/2026

Principal diagnosis: tuberculous meningitis
Other: HIV with viremia; opioid use disorder on buprenorphine; history of IV drug use
Allergies: NKDA

Presentation: 33-year-old man with two weeks of worsening headache with fever, vomiting, light sensitivity and a stiff neck. Prior admissions for septic arthritis (2024) and wound botulism (2025). T 38.6 C, HR 102. Drowsy but oriented to person, place and time. Neck stiff with a positive Brudzinski sign. Fundi without papilledema. Cranial nerves intact; no focal neurologic deficit.

CT head: mild hydrocephalus with basilar meningeal enhancement, no stroke.
CSF: WBC 150/uL, 80% lymphocytes; protein 100 mg/dL; glucose 20 mg/dL (serum 90). Gram stain negative. AFB smear negative. TB nucleic acid amplification positive for M. tuberculosis, rifampin resistance not detected (05/06). Mycobacterial culture pending at discharge.
Chest x-ray normal. HIV-1 RNA 31,000, CD4 156.

Course: rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol with pyridoxine from 05/06. Dexamethasone IV, switched to oral and tapering over 8 weeks total. Neurosurgery reviewed the imaging; repeat CT 05/12 unchanged, no shunt needed as he improved clinically. Headache and fever resolved by the second week. ART changed because of rifampin interactions: dolutegravir 50 mg twice daily plus emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate daily. TMP-SMX DS daily added for pneumocystis prophylaxis (CD4 <200). Buprenorphine/naloxone continued 8/2 mg BID; monitor for withdrawal given rifampin.

Discharge medications:
1. rifampin 600 mg daily
2. isoniazid 300 mg daily
3. pyrazinamide 1500 mg daily
4. ethambutol 1200 mg daily
5. pyridoxine 50 mg daily
6. dexamethasone taper per schedule
7. dolutegravir 50 mg BID
8. emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 200/300 mg daily
9. TMP-SMX 800/160 mg daily
10. buprenorphine/naloxone 8/2 mg SL BID
11. naloxone nasal spray PRN

Disposition: home. Directly observed therapy arranged through the local health department TB program. ID clinic in 4-6 weeks. PCP follow-up.

documents.title: Call from inpatient team
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Inpatient ID team called to let us know pt is admitted with TB meningitis since 5/5, improving, expected home late May. They will continue his buprenorphine at discharge and send a summary. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: ID addendum: CSF culture
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Addendum to discharge summary of 05/29/2026, Brandon Crowley.
CSF mycobacterial culture from 05/05 grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. Susceptible to isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol and pyrazinamide. No change to the regimen. Health department notified.

documents.title: Health department TB program
documents.author: public health
documents.body:
Local Board of Health, Tuberculosis Control
Re: Brandon Crowley

This is to inform the primary care physician that the above patient is enrolled in directly observed therapy for tuberculosis as of 05/30/2026, with daily video-observed doses on weekdays and self-administered doses on weekends. Contact investigation is under way per protocol. Please direct questions to the TB nurse case manager.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hey doc im home from the hospital, they gave me films till the 25th. can you send the next ones to the same pharmacy. still taking all the TB pills, the nurse watches me on video lol

documents.title: Re: Refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're home, Brandon. Sent 4 weeks of the films to your pharmacy. If you start feeling withdrawal symptoms (the TB medicine can lower the buprenorphine level), call me, we can adjust. Keep going with the TB nurse.

documents.title: Infectious disease clinic follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Infectious Disease Clinic
Visit date: 07/08/2026
Re: Brandon Crowley

Follow-up for tuberculous meningitis (culture-confirmed, fully susceptible) and HIV. Taking all doses under DOT, none missed per health department. Headache gone. No fever, vomiting or vision change. Finished the dexamethasone taper.

Exam: alert and oriented, neck supple, no meningeal signs. Cranial nerves intact. No focal deficits. Gait normal.
Labs: liver tests normal. HIV-1 RNA 140 copies/mL (from 31,000), CD4 198.

Assessment: good response. Intensive phase completed 07/07/2026.
Plan:
- Stop pyrazinamide and ethambutol. Continue rifampin 600 mg and isoniazid 300 mg daily with pyridoxine for 10 more months (12 months total for CNS disease).
- Continue dolutegravir 50 mg BID + emtricitabine/TDF while on rifampin; switch back to single-tablet regimen two weeks after rifampin ends.
- Continue TMP-SMX until CD4 above 200 on two checks.
- Monthly LFTs. Return in 6 weeks.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Electronic request for buprenorphine/naloxone films. PDMP checked, on schedule. 4 weeks sent. ID clinic letter of 7/8 reviewed and filed. Pt overdue for an office visit; asked front desk to reach out to schedule once his TB clinic schedule allows.
